## Getting the Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(ggthemes)
ai_salary <- read_csv('data/raw/ai_salary_majors.csv')
major_occupations <- read_csv('data/raw/major_occupations.csv')

```


## Exploring the Data

```{r}
# A breif overview of the data
head(ai_salary)
str(ai_salary)
head(major_occupations)
str(major_occupations)


ai_salary |> 
  summarise(max = max(ai_exposure_percentile), min = min(ai_exposure_percentile), mean = mean(ai_exposure_percentile))
```

```{r}
#A look at variables of interest
ai_salary |> 
  group_by(broad_field_short) |> 
  mutate(amount = n()) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(ai_exposure_percentile >= 75) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = ai_exposure_percentile, fill = fct_reorder(broad_field_short, ai_exposure_percentile))) +
  geom_boxplot()

Q4_percentile_ai_salary <- ai_salary |> 
  group_by(broad_field_short) |> 
  mutate(amount = n(), median_sal_by_field = mean(median_starting_salary)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(ai_exposure_percentile >= 75)

```


> Interesting, here are the feilds that are in the 75th percentile and up, ai seems to impact a wide range of feilds from english to competer science. 

```{r}
# We have to first make a var that shows if the cafe is rural, suburban, urban
q1 <- quantile(Q4_percentile_ai_salary$median_starting_salary, 0.25, na.rm = T)
q3 <- quantile(Q4_percentile_ai_salary$median_starting_salary, 0.75, na.rm = T)

new_Q4_percentile_ai_salary <- Q4_percentile_ai_salary |> 
  group_by(broad_field_short) |> 
  mutate(starting_salary_Low = (median_sal_by_field < q1), 
         starting_salary_Med = ((q1 <= median_sal_by_field) & (median_sal_by_field <= q3)),
         starting_salary_High = (median_sal_by_field > q3)) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(starting_salary_Low, starting_salary_Med, starting_salary_High), names_to = "salary", names_prefix = "starting_salary_", values_to = "yes_no") |> 
  filter(yes_no == T)
dim(Q4_percentile_ai_salary) 
new_Q4_percentile_ai_salary
  
```

> Now we have three levels of salary: high, med, low

> Is there a difference in the relationship between median starting salary years and ai exposure?

```{r fig.height=10}
new_Q4_percentile_ai_salary |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = ai_exposure, y=fct_reorder(broad_field_short, ai_exposure))) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  facet_wrap(~salary, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")

# Attempt 1

new_Q4_percentile_ai_salary |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = ai_exposure, y=fct_reorder(broad_field_short, ai_exposure))) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  facet_wrap(~fct_relevel(salary, c("High", "Med", "Low")), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(title = "Fields Most Exposed to AI", subtitle = "Highest AI exposure to fields, by starting salary level", y="", x="AI Exposure", caption = "By: Andrew Lamb, Created:10/27/26, Data:AI Salary Majors, TidyTuesday 10/20/26")+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"), plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))


```

```{r fig.height=10}
# Attempt 2
library(ggridges)
library(janitor)


new_Q4_percentile_ai_salary |> 
  get_dupes(broad_field_short, salary) |> 
  filter(broad_field_short %in% c("Mathematics & Statistics", "Philosophy & Religion", "Interdisciplinary", "English", "Theology & Religion", "Business", "Education", "Physical Sciences", "Social Sciences", "Foreign Languages")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = ai_exposure, y=fct_reorder(broad_field_short, ai_exposure), fill = fct_relevel(salary, c("High", "Med", "Low")))) +
  geom_density_ridges(scale = 1)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("forestgreen", "green", "lightgreen"))+
  labs(title = "Distribution of AI Exposure by Field Separated by Salary level", subtitle = "AI exposure is disproportionately affecting low starting salary fields, such as Philosophy, English, Religion more than higher starting salary fields such as Business and Foreign Languages", y="", x="Density of AI Exposure", caption = "By: Andrew Lamb, Created:10/27/26, Data:AI Salary Majors, TidyTuesday 10/20/26
*Salary: Low = 0-25 Perecntile, Med = 25-75 Perecntile, High = 75-100 Perecntile out of the reported starting salary in the data", fill = "Salary*")+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0), plot.title = element_text(hjust = -0.1, face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = -0.72))

ggsave("tt_10_27_6.png")
```

Perecntile out of the reported starting salary in the data", fill = "Salary*")+

> The graph shows the feilds that have a med starting income have more fields effected then the low and high salary starting pay jobs. This may be due to the fact that most jobs will fall in the middle of the distabution. This is still interesting to consider. Especially since historicaly big leaps in technonlgy disporpotialy effect work class people.  

## Conclusion

> It seems that AI is effecting almost all fields no matter what you major in college, but the effects might not be equal.
